items.fix: Add a "Reset all reading settings" button that confirms and announces the result in the status region. Add "Delete my saved reading settings" that removes them from the account API, the `rp` cookie and vendor systems. State the retention period next to the settings.
items.impact: Returning to a known good state means re-ticking every option from memory. A record implying a disability stays against the card number with no visible retention period and no self-service erasure. This adds memory load and denies control over sensitive data.
items.problem: There is no reset-to-standard control and no way to delete the stored preferences. The panel does not say how long settings are kept. Because the form does not load saved values, the reader cannot see what is stored. There is a single submit button and no reset or delete code.
items.where: settings.html form (only one button, `<button type="submit">Save settings</button>`); integration.md bullet 5, "The account API stores the same settings against the library card number"

items.fix: Limit adaptation to book content by an explicit path allowlist. Never adapt service pages, the accessibility statement, the privacy notice, or sign-in and account pages. Make personalised responses uncacheable, or key them on preference values with `Vary` set.
items.impact: Affected readers could be unable to reach, or could receive altered versions of, the documents explaining the processing. Readers who chose neither mode could get a degraded page with no explanation. Affects screen reader and simplified-text users most.
items.problem: Nothing limits stripping of "decorative sidebars" (`sr=1`) or rewriting (`level=simplified`) to book chapters. On "every request" the edge could strip the header and footer (account status, Accessibility and Privacy links) or rewrite the privacy notice and accessibility statement into simplified text. Nothing says whether edge-adapted pages are cached per user or by header (`Vary`), so one reader's adapted page could be served to another. The footer links are the only route to the statement and notice.
items.where: integration.md bullet 1 (the cookie "is read at the edge on every request"), bullets 2 and 3; settings.html `<footer>` links `Accessibility` and `Privacy`

items.fix: Apply settings from the account at sign-in, server side, not only from a device cookie. Honour OS preferences before sign-in. Offer session-only text size and contrast controls on public pages including sign-in. When saved settings are not active, say so with a link to apply them.
items.impact: Low-vision, motion-sensitive and dyslexic readers, especially on shared computers, must use sign-in and navigation without needed adjustments. Settings "saved to your library account" silently fail to apply, contradicting the panel text.
items.problem: Text size, contrast and motion settings apply only after sign-in and only in a browser holding the `rp` cookie, which only the panel's script sets. The sign-in page, signed-out catalogue browsing, and browsers that block or clear cookies get defaults. Cookies are often cleared on library public PCs and in private browsing. Nothing tells the reader their saved settings are not applied.
items.where: Case description ("Signed-in readers can set…"); settings.html header "Signed in as reader…"; integration.md bullet 1 (adaptation keyed on the `rp` cookie)

items.fix: Anchor bookmarks and highlights to the original text and keep the original's page and location markers in any alternative view. Never leave orphaned note markers. Keep notes as described in an earlier finding on notes. Until locations can be mapped between versions, warn readers before they switch.
items.impact: Saved places land in the wrong spot or are lost, quotes and page numbers do not match a classmate's copy or a citation, and note links go nowhere or are announced with no target. Readers cannot tell whether the fault lies in the book, the service or their settings. Affects students, readers with cognitive disabilities and screen reader users.
items.problem: Replacing a chapter with model output, or removing footnotes and notes, changes the text that bookmarks, highlights, reading position, search and page references depend on. When notes are removed, in-text note markers are probably left pointing at nothing. Nothing says how these features behave across versions or across devices with different settings. integration.md describes whole-chapter replacement and footnote removal with no handling of locations or references.

items.fix: Put the links in a list and draw the separators with CSS, or wrap them in `<span aria-hidden="true">`.
items.impact: It adds a little noise to every page for screen reader users.
items.problem: The middle dot is literal text, so some screen readers at some punctuation settings announce it as "middle dot" or "dot".
